hints: For each interval, count earlier intervals whose right endpoint reaches at least its right endpoint.
In a start-ascending, end-descending order, process equal left endpoints together so equal intervals count each other correctly.
A Fenwick tree over compressed right endpoints counts previous endpoints on either side.
analogy: For each range, count how many range endpoints lie far enough to contain it or be contained by it.
example: Among [1,6],[2,4],[3,5], the first contains two, while [2,4] is contained by one.
algorithm: Sort intervals and coordinate-compress right endpoints. Use Fenwick prefix counts while scanning groups to count contained intervals; reverse the order for containing counts, accounting for duplicate intervals as a group.
correctness: Each prior interval has a start no greater than the current one; comparing right endpoints then decides containment, and grouped duplicates ensure identical ranges include one another.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
